subject: DPA confirmation and onshore routing for LLM data

From: Suzanne Cho <suzanne.cho@hearthwell.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: procure@hearthwell.com, kevin.martin@hearthwell.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA confirmation and subprocessor onshore routing

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick call this morning. Procurement and security need a written confirmation on a couple of items before we proceed to signature:

1) No-training / model improvement: is Hearthwell data excluded from any model training or improvement pipelines by default? We need explicit contractual language and an implementation commitment.
2) Subprocessor list + residency: please share the current subprocessor list and confirm which subprocessors (if any) will have access to plaintext interactions. We need assurance that any subprocessors handling PHI or PII can be routed to US-only onshore KMS and storage.
3) Evidence pack: security needs a small evidentiary bundle (SOC 2 page, dataflow diagram, export controls for prompt/response IP). A zip or drive link is fine.

We're aiming for a final DPA by next week if the technical commitments are clear. Can you send the DPA redline and the subprocessor snapshot? Also note we may request a short amendment to explicitly call out prompt/response ownership and derivative restrictions.

Appreciate it —
Suzanne
Senior Procurement Manager
Hearthwell Inc.

--

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 12:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA confirmation and subprocessor onshore routing

Suzanne —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:

• No-training: Yes — by default we can commit to a contractual "no-training / no model improvement" promise for Hearthwell interactions. Operationally that maps to (a) a processing flag on your tenant to exclude data from training routes, (b) KV/prefix eviction and ephemeral logging for interactive sessions, and (c) an audit trace you can verify.

• Subprocessors & residency: Attaching the current subprocessor snapshot. We have a small set of subprocessors (cloud IaaS, telemetry processing, logging) and an onshore KMS partner for US-only keys. When you select the US-residency option in the DPA, we route all plaintext handling through the US KMS and onshore storage; subprocessors that require cross-border transfers are excluded from that routing.

• Evidence pack: Attached is a starter bundle (DPA draft, subprocessor list). Neha will follow with operational proof items (SOC page references, dataflow diagram, export control statement).

Next steps we propose:
1) I attach redwood_dpa_v3.pdf with an explicit Section 4.2 "No Model Training" clause and Section 7 listing routing controls. Please review and flag any redlines.
2) If legal wants prompt/response ownership language stronger than the standard, point them to Section 5.1 — we can add an explicit "Customer owns outputs and derivative rights" paragraph.
3) Lauren (cc) will coordinate procurement/legal signature and the DocuSign envelope once terms are set.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_v3.pdf, subprocessor_list_202602.pdf

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0113

Hi Suzanne —

Following Marcus' note, here's a concise ops/evidence summary you can share with security:

1) Operational enforcement: a tenant-level "no-train" flag implemented at the request router. When enabled, interactions are tagged and excluded from our model improvement pipelines and from any offline training stores.

2) KMS + residency: we support a US-onshore KMS key configuration (customer-managed or Redwood-managed HSM). For onshore customers we configure the key to enforce that objects and decrypted payloads stay in US regions.

3) Subprocessor access: subprocessors that perform telemetry or telemetry-storage are limited to hashed telemetry only. Only the onshore KMS partner and our in-region compute pool have access to decrypted plaintext. The current list (attached) flags which processors are eligible for onshore routing.

4) Evidence pack: attached ops_evidence_pack_202602.zip (contains SOC 2 compliance page, high-level dataflow diagram, redacted export-control statement, and a short runbook snippet showing the no-train toggle audit logs).

If security wants a live walkthrough we can schedule a 30-min session and share a time-based readout proving the no-train flag was active for a short test tenant.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
